exposure: postplacental levonorgestrel intrauterine device (LNG-IUD) insertion program maturity
method of insertion (manual vs. ring-forceps) after vaginal delivery
cohort: The study included 235 women who received postplacental levonorgestrel intrauterine device (LNG-IUD) insertions as part of an academic program between January 2016 and December 2018.
finding: LNG-IUD expulsion rates significantly decreased after the first program year, suggesting that program maturity may be associated with a lower expulsion risk.
mod_finding: After vaginal delivery, manual insertion of the LNG-IUD was associated with a higher expulsion rate than ring-forceps insertion.
